findings.claim: The parenthetical 'a review has landed that late, after the merge' asserts a post-merge REVIEW the cited doctrine record does not contain: bot-protocols.md @16c5694 § Invocation says CodeRabbit 'acknowledged twelve minutes late, past the merge, on mmnto-ai/totem-strategy#1182' — an acknowledgement, not a review. The diff upgraded an ack to a review in text shipped to every consumer.
findings.counterexample: gh api repos/mmnto-ai/totem-strategy/pulls/1182/reviews returns ONE review (gemini-code-assist[bot], 2026-09-01T18:42:41Z); pulls/1182/comments is empty; CodeRabbit's 18:50:07Z issue comment says 'Action not completed / Pull request is closed' — merge was 18:48:52Z. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): the parenthetical removed; the window reads 'about 12 minutes from the trigger'.

findings.claim: 'never the head's green status' was a blanket over all bots justified by CodeRabbit alone, dropping the doctrine's carve: Greptile's green `Greptile Review` check run does mark the sha it reviewed; GCA posted neither a status nor a check run (§ Working the findings). Broader in prohibition than the doctrine.
findings.counterexample: A seat on a Greptile round sees the green check run on the head — doctrine: confirmation; the old text: not confirmation, another trigger spent. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): 'never a green commit status on the head' with both carve-outs stated.

findings.claim: 'never a re-invoke folded into another comment' redefined the doctrine's contrast term: re-invoke is the cadence's word (re-invoke only for risky rework, reason recorded in the round comment); the doctrine's claim is cadence accounting (the standalone re-trigger IS the first pass), not a comment-shape rule.
findings.counterexample: A seat whose trigger chat-routed reads the old tail and either records a risky-rework reason it does not owe, or concludes a standalone re-invoke needs no word. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): 'that bot's first pass, not a re-invoke, which the cadence reserves for risky rework with the reason recorded in the round comment'.

findings.claim: Trigger ownership stated two ways in one paragraph: 'the operator's to post' at the opening, then 'a standalone re-trigger on the operator's word' (an on-the-word form that reads as the seat posting). The distributed AGENTS floor (init-templates.ts:2996) says triggers are the maintainer's to post, never an agent's.
findings.counterexample: One paragraph, two owners of the same act. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): 'a standalone re-trigger, posted by the operator on the same terms'.

findings.claim: 'about 12 minutes' is the doctrine's bound but the text never said what the window is measured FROM.
findings.counterexample: On mmnto-ai/totem-strategy#1182 the bound is trigger (18:38:07Z) to acknowledgement (18:50:07Z) = 12m00s; the merge was 10m45s after the trigger. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): 'about 12 minutes from the trigger'.

findings.claim: The compression of 'it settles green either way' dropped the doctrine's discriminator ('Review completed' on the sha it reviewed, 'Review skipped: automatic reviews are disabled' on every push head it did not) — the one readable status-surface signal the doctrine documents.
findings.counterexample: Head shows CodeRabbit green / 'Review completed' — doctrine: that is the sha it reviewed; the old text: green tells you nothing. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): the discriminator stated in the parenthetical.

findings.claim: The diff added a distributed contract clause set with zero new assertions: the three existing mechanisms (constant equals the .claude copy; every constant matches its .agents twin; no banned term) all pass if the whole section is deleted from all three copies at once.
findings.counterexample: Delete the section from the constant and both copies: init.test.ts + config-drift.test.ts stay at 387 passed. FOLDED (4e80e3a8): a lock test on the section's presence, its position before Phase 1, the three clauses and the fenced read.
